label: <DEL> step or original-phase 3 input, in sequences containing several of {1,m,0,n,z,j}
explanation: Fires almost entirely at two kinds of step. One is the <DEL> step (about 47% of mass, 6% firing rate there). The other is original-phase inputs, mainly the digit 3 (31% of mass, 8x lift), with weaker contributions from q, g, v and l. The copy phase is nearly silent (5% of mass). Whether it fires depends on what is already in the prefix: rates are much higher when the earlier tokens include 1, m, 0 or n (first_tok=1 gives 6.3x lift), and when the sequence has more digits and is longer (L=9, later positions). This reads like a distributed readout of stored token identity rather than one clean trigger. The strongest activations are a 3 input late in the original phase, or <DEL>, after a prefix that starts with 1. Never fires at t=0 or once the copy has gone wrong. Precision is low (most <DEL> and 3 steps do not fire), so the predicate captures where activation mass sits, not a sufficient condition.
